title: Operation Strix
summary: A book whose form changes how it is read and by whom. A field manual for a spy who has to pass as an ordinary father, with the secrets hidden in plain sight.
coverAlt: An ordinary parenting handbook with a hidden second text in its margins

blocks.heading: The idea
blocks.body: From the outside it is a dull parenting handbook. Inside, a second text runs in the margins in a second ink that appears only under a red lens. One book, two readers.

blocks.label: Research. Real field manuals, school handbooks, and how each one organizes instructions.

blocks.heading: Process
blocks.body: The hard part was making the parenting advice good enough to stand alone. If it read as a disguise, the book failed. I wrote and set both texts together, spread by spread, so every page holds two honest readings.

blocks.caption: The same spread, with and without the red lens.
Risograph proofs of the hidden margin ink.

blocks.text: A good disguise has to be true.

blocks.heading: Reflection
blocks.body: Readers found the second text faster than I expected, and that was the lesson. Hiding something well is a typography problem, not a printing trick.
